featherdrop is now **zero-knowledge**: files are end-to-end encrypted in your browser before they ever leave it, so the server only ever stores opaque ciphertext — it can't read your files, their names, or their types, even if it wanted to. This is a breaking change to the crypto model; read the upgrade note below.

## Added

- **Zero-knowledge (end-to-end) encryption.** The browser encrypts every file with `XChaCha20-Poly1305` (libsodium `crypto_secretstream`, 64 KiB chunks) before upload. The content key never reaches the server: in link mode it lives only in the URL `#fragment` (never sent in a request line); in password mode it's wrapped with an Argon2id-derived key and only the wrapped blob is stored. The filename and content type are encrypted inside the blob too — the server sees nothing but ciphertext and its length.
- **Arbitrary file size.** Encryption streams through the Origin Private File System (OPFS) and uploads resumably with tus, so size is bounded by disk, not RAM. Downloads decrypt and stream to disk through a service worker. Older browsers without OPFS/streaming fall back to an in-memory path with a size cap and a clear message.
- **Fully client-side inline preview.** Images and PDFs preview on the download page by decrypting in the browser and rendering from an in-memory `blob:` URL — the server no longer serves any inline route. The inert-type allowlist (raster images + PDF only; never SVG/HTML) is enforced on the decrypted blob.

## Changed

- **Server is now a dumb ciphertext store.** It stores and serves the opaque blob verbatim, enforces expiry and the download limit/burn, and never performs any cryptography. The `GET` download response is raw bytes — no key or password ever appears in a request to the server.
- **Privacy copy updated** across the app, README, and template to the zero-knowledge claim, superseding the earlier "encrypted at rest" wording.

## Removed

- **Server master-key mode is gone.** Decryption that the server could perform with its own key contradicts the zero-knowledge model. New shares are link mode (key in the `#fragment`) or password mode only.

## Upgrade notes

- **Existing (v1) links keep working until they expire.** Old shares are read with the previous scheme; the data model is dual-format and the migration is additive, so no action is needed on upgrade. Same ports, same `/data` volume, same configuration.
- **The key is in the link.** A zero-knowledge link only decrypts if the whole URL — including the part after `#` — is copied. A truncated link can't be recovered, by design: the server never had the key.

## Under the hood

- New isolated client modules: `lib/e2e/crypto.ts` (crypto core), `blob-layout.ts` (framed blob format), `opfs-scratch.ts`, `stream-download.ts` + `public/sw-download.js`, `pipeline.ts`, and the upload/download flows — each unit-tested in Node + libsodium with a full encrypt→blob→decrypt round-trip.
- A new CI end-to-end test starts the built app and drives a real browser through encrypt → upload → share link → decrypt → download, asserting byte-identical output and a working inline preview on every push.
